title: Semantically-aware KV compaction with bounded-staleness contracts
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Goal: Introduce a semantically-aware compaction layer for the KV cache that reclaims GPU memory proactively while providing formal bounded-staleness guarantees to the serving runtime. This ticket designs the correctness contract, implementation approach, and rollout plan for a compaction policy that uses prefix affinity, semantic groupings (based on prefix hierarchies and request heuristics), and TTL-like levers to make eviction decisions that preserve model correctness for ongoing decode sessions.
motivation: Current LRU/TTL heuristics cause either unnecessary memory pressure (over-retention) or correctness regressions for long-lived generation sessions that reuse prefixes. We need a middle ground that reclaims memory predictably without breaking K/V cache assumptions for in-flight decodes or streaming continuations.
background: Previous work includes prefix-scoped deterministic eviction and hybrid TTL+LRU schemes. This ticket differs by formalizing a bounded-staleness contract (expressed as 'max safe staleness in steps') and pairing it with semantic compaction that coalesces keys with strong prefix affinity for bulk reclamation, reducing metadata churn on the GPU.
design_overview: Contract: entries annotated with safe_staleness=N mean they may be compacted or reclaimed only if no active decode pipeline requires staleness <= N. Compaction preserves a compacted summary that can be rehydrated lazily with a bounded cost.
Semantic grouping: cluster KV entries by (model_id, prefix_hash_bucket, sequence_length_bucket, certainty_score bucket) to allow bulk compaction that keeps frequently co-accessed keys together.

Compaction vs eviction: compaction produces a memory-light summary (e.g., quantized or lossy fingerprint + short continuation state) instead of immediate eviction; eviction remains for entries that exceed TTL or are safely recoverable.
Rehydration: a low-overhead path to reconstruct compacted entries when a decode requests them; this path is rate-limited to avoid thundering herd into CPU/GPU IO.

Safety invariant: for any active decode with prefix P, the runtime must ensure either the full KV entries are present or the safe_staleness of compacted entries for that prefix >= remaining_decode_steps.
acceptance_criteria: Specification docs that define the bounded-staleness contract and per-prefix invariants reviewed and approved by Applied ML and Runtime teams.
Prototype compaction implemented in the runtime (config flag off by default) with unit tests verifying invariants under synthetic workloads.
Microbenchmarks demonstrating <=10% added latency on first rehydration and >=18% reduction in steady-state GPU KV memory for mixed long/short session workloads.
E2E regression tests showing no more than P0-level loss in output quality (BLEU/ROUGE proxies for generation quality on eval prompts) when compaction is enabled under target workloads.
Telemetry: new metrics exported (compactions/sec, rehydrations/sec, average safe_staleness, reclaimed_gpu_bytes) and dashboards added to Console.
Rollout plan documented with kill-switch and gradual ramping thresholds.
Canary in Dedicated environment for one week with live traffic and manual sign-off from Reliability and ML infra teams.
implementation_plan: Phase 1 (spec + model): draft contract and API annotations for KV entries; add safe_staleness metadata field to cache index.
Phase 2 (prototype): implement grouping and compaction serialization format; add rehydration logic behind a flag; add unit tests and microbench harness.
Phase 3 (perf): benchmark memory vs latency tradeoffs; tune group sizes and rehydrate rate limits; add GPU memory accounting hooks.
Phase 4 (safety): add invariants checks in dev builds that assert correctness under simulated concurrency; create regression suite that runs nightly.
Phase 5 (rollout): enable canary; monitor metrics; iterate on thresholds and provide rollback if rehydration overload observed.
Expected owners: Marco Li (runtime), Priya Shah (applied-ml review), Omar Reyes (observability).
tests: Unit tests for compaction/rehydration correctness using deterministic pseudo-random workloads.
Concurrency fuzz tests to detect races between compaction and active decode pipelines.
Synthetic workload sweep: short-only, long-only, mixed; measure memory and 95th/99th latency.
Quality evals: run existing generation eval set to ensure no model quality regressions beyond defined threshold.
Chaos tests: simulate node OOM and ensure compaction fallback doesn't cause correctness loss.
Integration test in Dedicated with limited capacity to validate rehydration rate limiting under load.
metrics: active_decode_safe_staleness_percent (fraction of decodes satisfied without rehydration)
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: rehydration storms could overload GPU/IO. Mitigation: aggressive rate limiting, token-bucket per model, and fallback to full eviction paths with circuit breaker metrics.
Risk: semantic grouping might accidentally coalesce unrelated keys causing performance cliff. Mitigation: conservative grouping thresholds and feature-flagged A/B experiments before full rollout.
Risk: formal contract misunderstood by caller code. Mitigation: contract enforced by runtime assertions in dev builds and clear API docs with examples.
Risk: increased complexity in memory accounting. Mitigation: add per-group accounting and reconcile in nightly job; introduce debug endpoints to inspect group membership.
rollout_plan: Stage 0: internal dev cluster testing for 2 weeks.
Stage 1: Dedicated canary with 5% of traffic for 7 days; observe rehydration and latency metrics.
Stage 2: Ramp to 25% after sign-off; keep canary guardrails for 72 hours.
Stage 3: Gradual global rollout if no regressions; maintain 1-hour rollback window via flag.
Kill-switch: runtime exposes 'force_disable_compaction' per-tenant for emergency rollback.
